Cephalexin Counseling: I counseled the patient regarding use of cephalexin as an antibiotic for prophylactic and/or therapeutic purposes. Cephalexin (commonly prescribed under brand name Keflex) is a cephalosporin antibiotic which is active against numerous classes of bacteria, including most skin bacteria. Side effects may include nausea, diarrhea, gastrointestinal upset, rash, hives, yeast infections, and in rare cases, hepatitis, kidney disease, seizures, fever, confusion, neurologic symptoms, and others. Patients with severe allergies to penicillin medications are cautioned that there is about a 10% incidence of cross-reactivity with cephalosporins. When possible, patients with penicillin allergies should use alternatives to cephalosporins for antibiotic therapy.

options.textAreaValue: Arava Counseling:  Patient counseled regarding adverse effects of Arava including but not limited to nausea, vomiting, abnormalities in liver function tests. Patients may develop mouth sores, rash, diarrhea, and abnormalities in blood counts. The patient understands that monitoring is required including LFTs       and blood counts.  There is a rare possibility of scarring of the liver and lung problems that can occur when taking methotrexate. Persistent nausea, loss of appetite, pale stools, dark urine, cough, and shortness of breath should be reported immediately. Patient advised to discontinue Arava treatment and consult with a physician prior to attempting conception. The patient will have to undergo a treatment to eliminate Arava from the body prior to conception.

Clofazimine Counseling:  I discussed with the patient the risks of clofazimine including but not limited to skin and eye pigmentation, liver damage, nausea/vomiting, gastrointestinal bleeding and allergy.

Colchicine Counseling:  Patient counseled regarding adverse effects including but not limited to stomach upset (nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, or diarrhea).  Patient instructed to limit alcohol consumption while taking this medication.  Colchicine may reduce blood counts especially with prolonged use.  The patient understands that monitoring of kidney function and blood counts may be required, especially at baseline. The patient verbalized understanding of the proper use and possible adverse effects of colchicine.  All of the patient's questions and concerns were addressed.

Dapsone Counseling- I discussed with the patient the risks of dapsone including but not limited to hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, rashes, methemoglobinemia, kidney failure, peripheral neuropathy, headaches, GI upset, and liver toxicity.  Patients who start dapsone require monitoring including baseline LFTs and weekly CBCs for the first month, then every month thereafter.  The patient verbalized understanding of the proper use and possible adverse effects of dapsone.  All of the patient's questions and concerns were addressed.
Gabapentin Counseling: I discussed with the patient the risks of gabapentin including but not limited to dizziness, somnolence, fatigue and ataxia.
Glycopyrrolate Counseling:  I discussed with the patient the risks of glycopyrrolate including but not limited to skin rash, drowsiness, dry mouth, difficulty urinating, and blurred vision.

Low Dose Naltrexone Counseling- I discussed with the patient the potential risks and side effects of low dose naltrexone including but not limited to: more vivid dreams, headaches, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, fatigue, dizziness, and anxiety.

Niacinamide Counseling: I recommended taking niacin or niacinamide, also know as vitamin B3, twice daily. Recent evidence suggests that taking vitamin B3 (500 mg twice daily) can reduce the risk of actinic keratoses and non-melanoma skin cancers. Side effects of vitamin B3 include flushing and headache.

NSAID Counseling: I discussed with the patient that NSAIDs should be taken with food. Prolonged use of NSAIDs can result in the development of stomach ulcers.  Patient advised to stop taking NSAIDs if abdominal pain occurs.  The patient verbalized understanding of the proper use and possible adverse effects of NSAIDs.  All of the patient's questions and concerns were addressed.

Olanzapine Counseling- I discussed with the patient the common side effects of olanzapine including but are not limited to: lack of energy, dry mouth, increased appetite, sleepiness, tremor, constipation, dizziness, changes in behavior, or restlessness.  Explained that teenagers are more likely to experience headaches, abdominal pain, pain in the arms or legs, tiredness, and sleepiness.  Serious side effects include but are not limited: increased risk of death in elderly patients who are confused, have memory loss, or dementia-related psychosis; hyperglycemia; increased cholesterol and triglycerides; and weight gain.

Oral Minoxidil Counseling- I discussed with the patient the risks of oral minoxidil including but not limited to shortness of breath, swelling of the feet or ankles, dizziness, lightheadedness, unwanted hair growth and allergic reaction.  The patient verbalized understanding of the proper use and possible adverse effects of oral minoxidil.  All of the patient's questions and concerns were addressed.

Otezla Counseling: The side effects of Otezla were discussed with the patient, including but not limited to worsening or new depression, weight loss, diarrhea, nausea, upper respiratory tract infection, and headache. Patient instructed to call the office should any adverse effect occur.  The patient verbalized understanding of the proper use and possible adverse effects of Otezla.  All the patient's questions and concerns were addressed.
Oxybutynin Counseling:  I discussed with the patient the risks of oxybutynin including but not limited to skin rash, drowsiness, dry mouth, difficulty urinating, and blurred vision.

Plaquenil Counseling:  I discussed with the patient that a baseline ophthalmologic exam is needed at the start of therapy and every year thereafter while on therapy. A CBC may also be warranted for monitoring.  The side effects of this medication were discussed with the patient, including but not limited to agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia, seizures, rashes, retinopathy, and liver toxicity. Patient instructed to call the office should any adverse effect occur.  The patient verbalized understanding of the proper use and possible adverse effects of Plaquenil.  All the patient's questions and concerns were addressed.

Propranolol Counseling:  I discussed with the patient the risks of propranolol including but not limited to low heart rate, low blood pressure, low blood sugar, restlessness and increased cold sensitivity. They should call the office if they experience any of these side effects.

SSKI Counseling:  I discussed with the patient the risks of SSKI including but not limited to thyroid abnormalities, metallic taste, GI upset, fever, headache, acne, arthralgias, paraesthesias, lymphadenopathy, easy bleeding, arrhythmias, and allergic reaction.
Thalidomide Counseling: I discussed with the patient the risks of thalidomide including but not limited to birth defects, anxiety, weakness, chest pain, dizziness, cough and severe allergy.

Tranexamic Acid Counseling:  Patient advised of the small risk of blood clots with tranexamic acid. This medication should not be taken concurrently with oral contraceptives. They were also instructed to call if they developed any nausea, vomiting or diarrhea. All of the patient's questions and concerns were addressed.

Valtrex Counseling: I discussed with the patient the risks of valacyclovir including but not limited to kidney damage, nausea, vomiting and severe allergy.  The patient understands that if the infection seems to be worsening or is not improving, they are to call.
